title: Local and affine criteria for flatness of a quasi-coherent sheaf over a scheme
explicit_hypotheses: f:X\to S is a morphism of schemes.
\mathcal F is a quasi-coherent \mathcal O_X-module.
equivalent_conditions: For every pair of affine open subschemes U\subseteq X and V\subseteq S with f(U)\subseteq V, the \mathcal O_S(V)-module \mathcal F(U) is flat.
There exists an open covering S=\bigcup_{j\in J}V_j, and for each j an open covering f^{-1}(V_j)=\bigcup_{i\in I_j}U_i, such that \mathcal F|_{U_i} is flat over V_j for all i,j.

There exists an affine open covering S=\bigcup_{j\in J}V_j, and for each j an affine open covering f^{-1}(V_j)=\bigcup_{i\in I_j}U_i, such that \mathcal F(U_i) is flat as an \mathcal O_S(V_j)-module for all i,j.
additional_conclusions: If these conditions hold, then for arbitrary open U\subseteq X and V\subseteq S with f(U)\subseteq V, the sheaf \mathcal F|_U is flat over V.
standalone_statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to S\) be a morphism of schemes and \(\mathcal F\) a quasi-coherent \(\mathcal O_X\)-module. The following four conditions are equivalent: (1) \(\mathcal F\) is flat over \(S\); (2) for all affine open \(U\subseteq X\), \(V\subseteq S\) with \(f(U)\subseteq V\), the module \(\mathcal F(U)\) is flat over \(\mathcal O_S(V)\); (3) \(S\) admits an open cover \(V_j\) such that each \(f^{-1}(V_j)\) admits an open cover \(U_i\) on which \(\mathcal F|_{U_i}\) is flat over \(V_j\); and (4) these covers can be chosen affine, with \(\mathcal F(U_i)\) flat over \(\mathcal O_S(V_j)\) for all \(i,j\). If the conditions hold, then \(\mathcal F|_U\) is flat over \(V\) for every pair of open subschemes \(U\subseteq X,V\subseteq S\) with \(f(U)\subseteq V\).
context_interpretation_notes: Kept all four equivalence clauses as the conclusion, not as four unrelated extra hypotheses.
The concluding assertion about arbitrary open restrictions is retained.
required_shared_term_definitions: flat quasi-coherent module over a scheme

title: Local and affine criteria for flatness of a scheme morphism
explicit_hypotheses: f:X\to S is a morphism of schemes.
equivalent_conditions: For every affine open U\subseteq X and affine open V\subseteq S with f(U)\subseteq V, the ring map \mathcal O_S(V)\to\mathcal O_X(U) is flat.
There is an open cover S=\bigcup_j V_j and, for each j, a covering f^{-1}(V_j)=\bigcup_i U_i by open subschemes for which U_i\to V_j is flat.
There is an affine open cover S=\bigcup_j V_j and, for each j, an affine open cover f^{-1}(V_j)=\bigcup_i U_i with each ring map \mathcal O_S(V_j)\to\mathcal O_X(U_i) flat.
additional_conclusions: When f is flat, for any open U\subseteq X and V\subseteq S with f(U)\subseteq V, the restriction f|_U:U\to V is flat.
standalone_statement_latex: For a morphism of schemes \(f:X\to S\), the following conditions are equivalent: (1) \(f\) is flat; (2) for every pair of affine open subschemes \(U\subseteq X,V\subseteq S\) with \(f(U)\subseteq V\), the ring homomorphism \(\mathcal O_S(V)\to\mathcal O_X(U)\) is flat; (3) \(S\) has an open cover \(V_j\) such that each \(f^{-1}(V_j)\) has an open cover \(U_i\) with \(U_i\to V_j\) flat; (4) these covers can be chosen affine with each \(\mathcal O_S(V_j)\to\mathcal O_X(U_i)\) flat. If these conditions hold, then \(f|_U:U\to V\) is flat for any open \(U,V\) with \(f(U)\subseteq V\).
context_interpretation_notes: Preserved the four-way equivalence as a single conclusion plus the moreover clause.

title: Flatness of a quasi-coherent sheaf under affine direct image
explicit_hypotheses: S is a scheme.
f:X\to Y is an affine morphism of S-schemes.
\mathcal F is a quasi-coherent \mathcal O_X-module.
conclusion_claims: \mathcal F is flat over S if and only if f_*\mathcal F is flat over S.
standalone_statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a scheme, \(f:X\to Y\) an affine morphism of schemes over \(S\), and \(\mathcal F\) a quasi-coherent \(\mathcal O_X\)-module. Then \(\mathcal F\) is flat over \(S\) if and only if \(f_*\mathcal F\) is flat over \(S\).
context_interpretation_notes: The relative base S is introduced explicitly and not confused with the target Y.
required_shared_term_definitions: flat quasi-coherent module over a scheme

title: Composition of pointwise flatness for quasi-coherent modules
explicit_hypotheses: X\to Y\to Z are morphisms of schemes.
\mathcal F is a quasi-coherent \mathcal O_X-module.
x\in X and y is its image in Y.
\mathcal F is flat over Y at x.
Y\to Z is flat at y.
conclusion_claims: \mathcal F is flat over Z at x.
standalone_statement_latex: Let \(X\to Y\to Z\) be morphisms of schemes, let \(\mathcal F\) be a quasi-coherent \(\mathcal O_X\)-module, and let \(x\in X\) with image \(y\in Y\). If \(\mathcal F\) is flat over \(Y\) at \(x\) and \(Y\to Z\) is flat at \(y\), then \(\mathcal F\) is flat over \(Z\) at \(x\).
context_interpretation_notes: The pointwise hypotheses are local to this lemma and must not persist to the next one.

title: Flat morphisms are closed under composition
explicit_hypotheses: X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}Z are morphisms of schemes.
f and g are flat.
standalone_statement_latex: Let \(X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}Z\) be flat morphisms of schemes. Then \(g\circ f:X\to Z\) is flat.
context_interpretation_notes: The previous lemma's F, x, and y are deliberately absent; its variables were scoped to its own environment.

title: Flatness of sheaves is preserved under arbitrary base change
explicit_hypotheses: f:X\to S and g:S'\to S are morphisms of schemes.
X'=X\times_S S' and g':X'\to X is the projection.
\mathcal F is a quasi-coherent \mathcal O_X-module.
x'\in X' and x=g'(x').
\mathcal F is flat over S at x.
conclusion_claims: (g')^*\mathcal F is flat over S' at x'.
additional_conclusions: If \mathcal F is flat over S at every point, then (g')^*\mathcal F is flat over S' globally.
standalone_statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to S\) and \(g:S'\to S\) be morphisms of schemes, let \(X'=X\times_S S'\), and let \(g':X'\to X\) be the projection. For any quasi-coherent \(\mathcal O_X\)-module \(\mathcal F\) and \(x'\in X'\) with \(x=g'(x')\), flatness of \(\mathcal F\) over \(S\) at \(x\) implies flatness of \((g')^*\mathcal F\) over \(S'\) at \(x'\). In particular, if \(\mathcal F\) is flat over \(S\), its pullback is flat over \(S'\).
context_interpretation_notes: Separated the pointwise implication from its global corollary.
required_shared_term_definitions: flat quasi-coherent module over a scheme

title: Flat morphisms are stable under base change
explicit_hypotheses: f:X\to S is a flat morphism of schemes.
g:S'\to S is an arbitrary morphism of schemes.
conclusion_claims: The projection f':X\times_S S'\to S' is flat.
standalone_statement_latex: If \(f:X\to S\) is a flat morphism of schemes and \(g:S'\to S\) is any morphism of schemes, then the base change \(X\times_S S'\to S'\) is flat.
context_interpretation_notes: Does not inherit F or the particular point x from the preceding base-change lemma.

title: Generalizations lift along flat morphisms of schemes
explicit_hypotheses: f:X\to S is a flat morphism of schemes.
conclusion_claims: For any specialization s'\leadsto s in S and x\in X with f(x)=s, there is a specialization x'\leadsto x in X with f(x')=s'.
standalone_statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to S\) be a flat morphism of schemes. Given points \(s',s\in S\) with \(s\) a specialization of \(s'\), and any point \(x\in X\) lying over \(s\), there exists a generalization \(x'\) of \(x\) lying over \(s'\).
context_interpretation_notes: Expanded the precise topology-defined meaning of 'generalizations lift'; the source definition is topology.tex:3615.
required_shared_term_definitions: specialization and generalization in a topological space

title: Flat morphisms locally of finite presentation are universally open
explicit_hypotheses: f:X\to Y is a flat morphism of schemes, locally of finite presentation.
conclusion_claims: Every base change f':X\times_Y Y'\to Y' is an open map of topological spaces.
standalone_statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to Y\) be a flat morphism of schemes which is locally of finite presentation. Then \(f\) is universally open: for every morphism \(Y'\to Y\), the base-changed morphism \(X\times_Y Y'\to Y'\) is open on underlying topological spaces.
context_interpretation_notes: Made 'universally open' explicit without borrowing any temporary hypotheses.

title: Universal openness from a flat finite-type sheaf with full support
explicit_hypotheses: f:X\to Y is a morphism of schemes locally of finite presentation.
\mathcal F is a finite-type quasi-coherent \mathcal O_X-module.
\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)=X.
\mathcal F is flat over Y.
standalone_statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to Y\) be a morphism of schemes locally of finite presentation and \(\mathcal F\) a finite-type quasi-coherent \(\mathcal O_X\)-module. If \(\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)=X\) and \(\mathcal F\) is flat over \(Y\), then \(f\) is universally open.
context_interpretation_notes: The original's 'f locally finite presentation' is rendered as locally of finite presentation; support is the entire underlying space.

title: Quasi-compact surjective flat morphisms induce quotient topologies
explicit_hypotheses: f:X\to Y is a quasi-compact, surjective, flat morphism of schemes.
T is an arbitrary subset of the underlying space of Y.
conclusion_claims: T is open in Y if and only if f^{-1}(T) is open in X.
T is closed in Y if and only if f^{-1}(T) is closed in X.
standalone_statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to Y\) be a quasi-compact, surjective, flat morphism of schemes. For any subset \(T\subseteq |Y|\), the subset \(T\) is open (respectively, closed) if and only if \(f^{-1}(T)\subseteq |X|\) is open (respectively, closed). Thus the continuous map \(|X|\to|Y|\) is a quotient map.
context_interpretation_notes: Converted the final 'submersive' clause into the equivalent quotient-topology formulation.
The superscript notations |X| and |Y| indicate underlying spaces.

title: Pointwise and global descent of flatness under flat pullback
explicit_hypotheses: S is a scheme, and h:X\to Y is a morphism of S-schemes.
\mathcal G is a quasi-coherent \mathcal O_Y-module.
x\in X, y=h(x), and h is flat at x.
conclusion_claims: \mathcal G is flat over S at y if and only if h^*\mathcal G is flat over S at x.
additional_conclusions: If h is globally flat and surjective, then \mathcal G is flat over S iff h^*\mathcal G is flat over S.
If h is flat and surjective and X is flat over S, then Y is flat over S.
standalone_statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a scheme, \(h:X\to Y\) a morphism of \(S\)-schemes, and \(\mathcal G\) a quasi-coherent \(\mathcal O_Y\)-module. Let \(x\in X\), \(y=h(x)\), and suppose \(h\) is flat at \(x\). Then \(\mathcal G\) is flat over \(S\) at \(y\) if and only if \(h^*\mathcal G\) is flat over \(S\) at \(x\). Consequently, if \(h\) is flat and surjective, global flatness of \(\mathcal G\) over \(S\) is equivalent to that of \(h^*\mathcal G\); moreover, if \(X\) is flat over \(S\), then \(Y\) is flat over \(S\).
context_interpretation_notes: Pointwise flatness of h at x is scoped to the first claim. Its global flat-and-surjective premise is repeated for both corollaries.
Avoids incorrectly carrying the pointwise x, y hypotheses as section-wide assumptions.
required_shared_term_definitions: flat quasi-coherent sheaf over a scheme

title: Scheme-theoretic support commutes with flat pullback
explicit_hypotheses: f:Y\to X is a flat morphism of schemes.
\mathcal F is a finite-type quasi-coherent \mathcal O_X-module.
Z\hookrightarrow X is the scheme-theoretic support of \mathcal F.
conclusion_claims: Y\times_X Z\hookrightarrow Y is the scheme-theoretic support of f^*\mathcal F.
standalone_statement_latex: Let \(f:Y\to X\) be a flat morphism of schemes and let \(\mathcal F\) be a finite-type quasi-coherent \(\mathcal O_X\)-module with scheme-theoretic support \(Z\hookrightarrow X\). Then the scheme-theoretic support of \(f^*\mathcal F\) is the closed subscheme \(Y\times_X Z\hookrightarrow Y\).
context_interpretation_notes: Clarified that inverse image of the closed subscheme means scheme-theoretic inverse image, not merely the topological preimage.

title: Flat inverse image preserves scheme-theoretically dense retrocompact opens
explicit_hypotheses: f:X\to Y is a flat morphism of schemes.
V\subseteq Y is an open subscheme that is retrocompact and scheme-theoretically dense.
standalone_statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to Y\) be a flat morphism of schemes and \(j:V\hookrightarrow Y\) a retrocompact open immersion that is scheme-theoretically dense, i.e. \(\mathcal O_Y\to j_*\mathcal O_V\) is injective. Then the inverse-image open subscheme \(f^{-1}(V)\subseteq X\) is scheme-theoretically dense in \(X\).
context_interpretation_notes: Expanded scheme-theoretic density into injectivity of the structure-sheaf map, while preserving the retrocompactness hypothesis.

title: Scheme-theoretic images commute with flat base change for quasi-compact maps
explicit_hypotheses: f:X\to Y is a flat morphism of schemes.
g:V\to Y is a quasi-compact morphism of schemes.
Z\hookrightarrow Y is the scheme-theoretic image of g.
Z'\hookrightarrow X is the scheme-theoretic image of V\times_Y X\to X.
conclusion_claims: Z' = X\times_Y Z as closed subschemes of X.
standalone_statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to Y\) be a flat morphism of schemes and \(g:V\to Y\) a quasi-compact morphism of schemes. Denote by \(Z\hookrightarrow Y\) the scheme-theoretic image of \(g\) and by \(Z'\hookrightarrow X\) the scheme-theoretic image of the base-changed map \(V\times_Y X\to X\). Then \(Z'=X\times_Y Z\) as closed subschemes of \(X\).
context_interpretation_notes: The original f^{-1}Z is unambiguously represented as the scheme-theoretic inverse image X×_Y Z.
